newsitem.title: USA: BASKETBALL-LSU COACH DALE BROWN STEPPING DOWN AFTER 25 YEARS.
newsitem.headline: BASKETBALL-LSU COACH DALE BROWN STEPPING DOWN AFTER 25 YEARS.

text.p: Disillusioned Louisiana State University basketball coach Dale Brown, who led the Tigers to four Southeastern Conference titles and 13 NCAA Tournament appearances in 25 years at the helm, announced his retirement Thursday, effective at the end of the season.

"When I became the head basketball coach at LSU, I had a dream of what I thought college athletics should be about, and now, after 25 years, that vision has become tarnished," said Brown, who noted that he was not pressured to quit.
The 61-year-old Brown, whose club has posted a mark of 7-6 mark this season, has a career record of 445-287 -- compiled entirely at LSU.
Brown led the Tigers to the Final Four in 1981 and 1986, but has failed to reach the tournament in four years.

LSU has struggled with three consecutive losing seasons, the first time that has happened to Brown. After winning at least 20 games in every season from 1989 to 1993, Brown has gone 35-48 in his last three full campaigns.
Brown turned the news conference announcing his retirement into a personal attack on the state of athletics.

"First, I'm deeply disappointed by the lack of committment by far too many athletes to get a good education," Brown said. "Part of this is our problem, due to the fact we have way too long of a season and will play a game any hour of the day or night to make a few bucks."

"Secondly, when I entered coaching 43 years ago, athletics was a component of education," he continued. "Today, it's about making money and winning big. There is a professional intensity creeping into intercollegiate sports. Losing a game does not make a person a loser.
"Thirdly, recruiting in its present state is absolutely ludicrous. In the early years, nobody enjoyed recruiting more than I did -- travelling and meeting outstanding young people and their families.

"Then, as fast as you can say 'Shazam,' it changed. Some high school and junior college players now have agents ... All of these things contribute to making athletes spoiled, expecting favours, think 'me' instead of 'we' and a kind of 'you can't touch me' attitude. We cannot dismiss athletes from the responsibility of their behaviour."

This season, the Tigers have been soundly beaten by three ranked foes, and also suffered an embarrassing home loss to Samford. LSU has won its last four games, however, including a 79-75 victory over Fresno State on Saturday.
Brown is second among SEC coaches in career wins, trailing only the legendary Adolph Rupp of Kentucky.

"The next 88 days of my life I will totally dedicate to this year's team," Brown said. "I am stimulated to work harder, be more focused and driven toward finishing this season ... one that will make everyone proud.
"I thank God for his guidance and today is not a sad day for me, but a happy one because retirement can be a rocking chair or a launching pad and I'm choosing the launching pad."
